subject.title: Telegram: Auto-reply to unauthorized group senders with admin contact instructions

question: Should Telegram add an opt-in, rate-limited group-denied-sender reply, and what default, ID disclosure, and admin-contact contract should it use?
rationale: The change turns a silent Telegram authorization denial into visible group output and may expose stable identifiers or amplify unauthorized traffic, so automation cannot safely choose the product/security contract.

options.title: Add Opt-In Notice
options.body: Add a Telegram plugin setting for a denied-sender onboarding reply with per-chat/topic/sender cooldown, configurable admin-contact wording, and explicit raw-ID behavior.

options.title: Route Through Operator Audit
options.body: Keep unauthorized senders silent and satisfy visibility through owner notification or denied-inbound audit work such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77546.

options.title: Keep Silent Denial
options.body: Decline sender-facing replies for now and keep logs, docs, and manual Telegram ID discovery as the supported secure posture.

recommendation.title: Add Opt-In Notice
recommendation.body: Add a Telegram plugin setting for a denied-sender onboarding reply with per-chat/topic/sender cooldown, configurable admin-contact wording, and explicit raw-ID behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current code, docs, and policy-history signal for the Telegram group authorization boundary this decision would change.
